items.title: The U.S. Is Burning Through Weapons in Iran. Russia and China Are Taking Note.
items.author: Anton Troianovski, Jonathan Swan, Eric Schmitt and Julian E. Barnes
items.content: <article>The Iran war has depleted U.S. weapons stockpiles, resulting in a significant erosion of firepower. A more drawn-out Iran conflict benefits Moscow and Beijing, some analysts say.</article>

items.title: A Top Scholar’s Fall Shows That Universities Don’t Get It
items.author: Jesse Singal
items.content: <article>By protecting a star from plagiarism charges, a storied college undermined its values.</article>

items.title: In Confirming Blanche, Senators Endorse a Justice Dept. Under Trump’s Sway
items.author: Glenn Thrush
items.content: <article>Time and again, Todd Blanche has made it clear that he believes President Trump possesses a nearly limitless right to directly control the actions of the Justice Department.</article>

items.title: Iran Issues List of Demands, Dampening Hopes of Reopening Strait of Hormuz
items.author: Yeganeh Torbati, Leily Nikounazar and Aaron Boxerman
items.content: <article>The head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said that the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until the United States met certain conditions.</article>

items.title: Yemen Teeters on Civil War as Regional Stability Hangs in the Balance
items.author: Ismaeel Naar and Aaron Boxerman
items.content: <article>While the Middle East waits to hear whether a deal can be reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the Yemeni government’s conflict with Iran-backed Houthi rebels escalated overnight.</article>

items.title: Amid Abuse Claims Against Max Miller, This Democrat Thinks He Can Win His Seat
items.author: Emily Davies
items.content: <article>Brian Poindexter, an ironworker, is in the spotlight in Ohio’s 7th Congressional District, where Mr. Miller faces multiple calls to step aside.</article>

items.author: Tim Balk
items.content: <article>The party is racing to get behind Dr. Abdul El-Sayed after a poisonous Senate primary in Michigan, but some Democrats still have reservations.</article>

items.title: Lindsey Graham Loved to Gab With Reporters. His Sister Won’t.
items.author: Michael Gold
items.content: <article>Senator Darline Graham, who took her brother’s place after his death and is now seeking to succeed him, has mostly declined to answer questions from reporters at the Capitol.</article>

items.author: Catie Edmondson
items.content: <article>The move came more than a month before the spending deadline, reflecting an eagerness in both parties to avoid a messy fight before the midterm elections.</article>

items.title: As Ukraine Strikes Wildberries, Russia’s Richest Businesswoman Faces Her Biggest Test Yet
items.author: Nataliya Vasilyeva, Paul Sonne, Alina Lobzina and Oleg Matsnev
items.content: <article>As Ukraine repeatedly strikes warehouses of the e-commerce site Wildberries, Tatyana Kim, its billionaire co-founder, faces her biggest test yet.</article>

items.title: What to Know About Wildberries, the Company in Ukraine’s Cross Hairs
items.author: Nataliya Vasilyeva
items.content: <article>Ukrainian drones have increasingly targeted warehouses belonging to Wildberries, which many Russians rely on as the country’s largest e-commerce business.</article>
